redFlags.title: Mark VIe advanced controls -- recurring lab and simulator failures (customer)
redFlags.text: O-CON33401 posted NPS -10 (n=10) and its sibling O-CON23401 dropped to 33 (n=6), both Mark VIe advanced courses run in the same Houston lab by the same instructor. The same signature recurs: virtualized simulators over wifi crashing every 2-3 minutes, lab A/C out for months, students moved to a wrong room on VR sims instead of real hardware, and login credentials that failed for over a day. Two customers wrote that the class was a waste of their money and one said they will not return to GE training. This matches the July signal on the O-CON134xx family -- a cross-month, cross-course equipment and facility problem, not instructor execution. The instructor was praised in the same surveys. Root cause: equipment / lab availability. This is past monitoring and into customer-refund and reputation territory.

redFlags.title: Steam Turbine Maintenance -- course structure and job relevance (E-STM10801)
redFlags.text: NPS 63 on a strong n=30, down from a 76 baseline. Instructors draw raves (Miller, Ogletree), so this is not an execution issue. The repeated theme is missing agenda and structure, and content pitched at outage-level maintenance that O&M techs won't perform day to day. Several asked for a course agenda and job-relevant scope. Root cause: course design. Worth a content review with the PLL rather than escalation -- a meaningful gap versus the monthly average, but a calm one.

redFlags.title: Internal delivery strong -- NPS 89, up 7 points month over month
redFlags.text: Internal NPS rose to 89 from 82 in July, and combined health is up to 85. Steam Turbine instructors in particular are rated near the ceiling, with several customer comments calling the delivery outstanding despite the course-design drag noted above. Leadership should see that the core delivery engine is healthy -- the flags this month are isolated equipment and content issues, not a systemic slide.

thisMonth.summary: August combined NPS came in at 85 on 324 responses, up from 82 in July. Internal led at 89 (137 responses) and customer held at 83 (187 responses). The month is healthy overall. Six courses flagged, but most are course-design or logistics items rather than alarms. One is serious: the Mark VIe advanced controls family.
bullets: Combined NPS 85, up 3 points from July; internal 89, customer 83.
O-CON33401 (Mark VIe Troubleshooting Advanced) is the critical flag at NPS -10 -- recurring equipment and facility failures, not instructor execution.
O-CON23401 (Mark VIe Maintenance Advanced) flagged at 33 in the same lab, confirming a Controls-lab pattern.
E-STM10801 (Steam Turbine Maintenance) at 63 on strong sample -- course-structure and job-relevance gap.
Two internal GT/GEN flags (I-GAS32301, I-CGEN20901) are thin-sample and driven by duration and summer-heat comments respectively -- watch, not act.

patterns.summary: The Mark VIe advanced controls courses have now failed on the same equipment and facility signature across multiple months. O-CON33401 has swung negative repeatedly (-25 in Sep 2024, -100 in Dec 2025, -10 now), and the July build flagged the same signature on the O-CON134xx family. This is a durable lab problem in Houston, not a bad cohort.
bullets: Mark VIe advanced (O-CON33401 / O-CON23401): recurring simulator, wifi, and lab-A/C failures across Dec 2025, June-July 2026, and August. Historical trend, not a one-off.
Untranslated Spanish and Portuguese comments on I-CGAS22001 point consistently at missing tools and materials -- real feedback a PLL can't act on until it's translated (see PL-004).
Steam Turbine Maintenance course-design signal (structure, job relevance) appears across multiple August sessions, not one class.

actions.text: Escalate the Mark VIe lab failures (O-CON33401 / O-CON23401) as a combined equipment and facility issue: hardwired simulators, working lab A/C, real-hardware access, and reliable credentials before the next scheduled advanced controls class.
actions.timing: Immediate -- before next Mark VIe advanced class

actions.text: Content review of E-STM10801 with the PLL: add a course agenda and re-scope toward the maintenance O&M techs actually perform, separating outage-level content.
Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on the processing machine so non-English comments translate. August left 8 untranslated, and the I-CGAS22001 tool/materials feedback is trapped in Spanish and Portuguese.

watchList: I-GAS32301 (GT Alstom Commissioning Expert) -- NPS 57, n=7. Course-duration driver low (5.6); students want more simulator time. Thin sample, monitor.
I-CGEN20901 (Craft H2 Generator) -- NPS 67, n=6. Comments are about summer heat, not the course. Drivers all 9+. Not actionable.
I-CGAS22001 (Craft Intermediate GT) -- NPS 75, n=20. Downward trend, but driven by tools/materials asks. Revisit once comments are translated.

thisMonth.summary: Internal NPS rose to 89 in August on 137 responses, up from 82 in July. The three internal flags are all thin-sample or non-course issues -- duration asks on the GT expert course, summer-heat complaints on the generator course, and a mild materials trend on Craft GT. Nothing here rises to escalation.
bullets: Internal NPS 89, up 7 points month over month.
I-GAS32301 (57, n=7): students want a longer course and more simulator time -- duration driver 5.6.
I-CGEN20901 (67, n=6): flagged, but the comments are about August heat, not the training.
I-CGAS22001 (75, n=20): downward trend tied to tools and materials, much of it in untranslated Spanish/Portuguese.

patterns.summary: Internal delivery is consistently strong. The recurring internal theme across GT courses is course duration and hands-on/simulator time -- students wanting more of a good thing, not quality problems. Instructor scores are uniformly high.
bullets: GT expert and craft courses repeatedly ask for more time and more simulator/hands-on work.
Materials and tools feedback on Craft GT recurs, largely from Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking cohorts.

actions.text: Review whether the GT Alstom Commissioning Expert course duration matches its scope -- multiple cohorts across years ask for more time on simulator.

watchList: I-CGEN20901 summer-heat comments -- facility comfort, not training. No action.
I-CGAS22001 tools/materials asks -- revisit once translated.

thisMonth.summary: Customer NPS held at 83 in August on 187 responses. The headline is the Mark VIe advanced controls failure -- O-CON33401 at -10 and O-CON23401 at 33, both from equipment and facility breakdowns in the Houston lab. E-STM10801 flagged on course structure. Outside those, customer sentiment is strong.
bullets: Customer NPS 83, roughly flat versus July's 82.
O-CON33401 at -10: crashing simulators, wifi, lab A/C out, wrong room -- customers threatening not to return.
O-CON23401 at 33: same lab, same instructor, same root cause.
E-STM10801 at 63 on n=30: course structure and job-relevance, strong instructors.

patterns.summary: The Mark VIe advanced controls lab has produced repeated negative customer months. This is a reputation and revenue risk -- customers are explicitly saying they paid for hardware training and got degraded VR simulators in a room without working A/C.
bullets: O-CON33401 negative or near-zero across Sep 2024, Dec 2025, and Aug 2026 -- durable equipment/facility failure.
Same signature now spans two course numbers (O-CON33401, O-CON23401) in the same lab.
Steam Turbine Maintenance content-relevance gap appears across multiple customer sites.

actions.text: Treat the Mark VIe lab as a customer-facing incident: fix simulators, A/C, hardware access, and credentials before the next advanced controls class, and consider proactive outreach to the August cohorts who asked for refunds.
Re-scope E-STM10801 toward O&M-relevant maintenance with a published agenda.

watchList: E-STM10801 -- confirm the content review lands; instructors are strong, so this is fixable with structure.

records.className: Site Manager Level 2 26-1
records.courseName: I-GIC30202 Site Manager Level 2
records.comment: This is revision A of this class  there are slides and work sheets that require revision and will be better before the next class. Of all the HLC classes I have taken I believe this is the best paced one  it slowed down at the end but was properly supplemented by final exam review which was quite helpful. This class references an old TKP installing frames that are no longer produced by GE. It has been discussed in class of updating some material to reflect the modern GE portfolio with a more recent project.  For someone like myself who has no installation experience  I would not recommend this class. As was stated during the course  this class is not technically inclined  it focuses much more on management aspects and overview topics. From what I'm aware  there are very few TKP across the world run by GE  but that is the primary project type this class focuses on. I've heard there will be more of these projects beginning in the US soon but currently  everything I've learned cannot be immediately applied to the TDI projects that are far more common.  For future reference  students should be told from day 1 to create their own folder in the student box and save all their case studies that are completed during class. There are a variety of SuccessFactor learning modules that are required in the class road map  some of which feel irrelevant to the class (HA Theory  GT & ST basics)  and the Documentum module needs redone if it's to be assigned to the next class. All students from this course attempted to complete that module but the exam in that curriculum contains questions that are not answered in the online course and are completely irrelevant to how the field operates now. The roadmap and MIS require updated before the next class  this class does not require the full 4 weeks that the MIS specifies. If possible  I would like the class to take 3 weeks  as the final exam currently takes place on a Monday. The class starting on Wednesday is also an odd choice in my opinion.

records.className: GE Steam Turbine to Alstom Steam Turbine (ST mechanical x-over) 26-2
records.courseName: I-XSTM30402 GE Steam Turbine to Alstom Steam Turbine (ST mechanical x-over)
records.comment: I would like to provide feedback regarding the steam turbine training instructor  as several issues negatively affected the overall learning environment and training experience.  English language proficiency The instructor’s English proficiency appears to be limited  which made it challenging at times to clearly understand the information being presented. Improving his English communication skills would help ensure that technical concepts and instructions are delivered more effectively to the class.  Unprofessional behavior toward the assistant instructor The instructor was at times rude  confrontational  and humiliating toward the assistant instructor in front of the entire classroom. This behavior did not reflect a professional standard and should be reviewed  as it undermined the learning atmosphere and classroom professionalism.  Lack of clear communication and structure There were noticeable communication issues throughout the course  including conflicting directions related to both technical content and course progression. The instructor often moved between topics without a clear structure or defined focus  which made it difficult for participants to follow the material and understand the intended learning objectives.  Unequal treatment of participants On at least one occasion  the instructor appeared discouraging toward a specific attendee whenever that person asked questions  while other participants were allowed to ask questions freely. This created a perception of unfair treatment and possible discrimination  which should not occur in a professional learning environment.  Emotional control and classroom conduct The instructor could demonstrate better emotional control in the classroom. On one occasion  he gathered the class and stated that he did not care if anyone had a personal issue with him  told those with concerns to email his manager  and threatened to leave and go home. This reaction was inappropriate for a professional training setting and created discomfort among the participants.  Overall comment Taken together  these issues created a toxic and uncomfortable learning environment that significantly affected the quality of the course. There is substantial room for improvement in future sessions  particularly in the areas of professionalism  communication  emotional conduct  and respectful engagement with both participants and fellow instructors.

records.courseName: I-XSTM30402 GE Steam Turbine to Alstom Steam Turbine (ST mechanical x-over)
records.comment: Strengths of the Current Program:  Daily Briefings: The morning classroom sessions at the start of the outage were highly effective. Discussing the day’s tasks and reviewing the specific components before disassembly provided crucial context that improved both safety and efficiency on the floor. This practice should certainly be maintained in future iterations. Opportunities for Improvement:  Test Debriefing: While the initial knowledge assessment was useful  I believe the training would be significantly improved if we conducted a group review of the test results. Going over the correct and incorrect answers would allow us to close knowledge gaps immediately and reinforce the technical concepts before moving further into the curriculum. Proposed Recommendation:  I recommend integrating a dedicated session to review the initial test immediately following the assessment. This could be structured as an open discussion to clarify common misconceptions or as a deep-dive into the specific Alstom turbine systems that caused the most confusion.

records.className: GE Steam Turbine to Alstom Steam Turbine (ST mechanical x-over) 26-2
records.courseName: I-XSTM30402 GE Steam Turbine to Alstom Steam Turbine (ST mechanical x-over)
records.comment: Some participants came with expectations that were outside the scope of this training. In the future  I would recommend selecting attendees based on the specific needs of the business and the TFA Training objectives  ensuring everyone is informed in advance that this is a hands-on  practical training. The hands-on sessions could be completed in less time if all participants arrived with the right mindset. Additionally  if the business needs to accommodate personnel from different roles or positions  it would be beneficial to offer a separate  role-specific course. During the training  there were instances of disrespectful behavior toward the instructor  which also impacted the overall experience for the other participants  as it limited the available time to fully cover and discuss deeper training topics. Overall  the training was well-structured and valuable. However  for our Steam Power segment  it would be highly beneficial to have a dedicated course focused on older/legacy machinery.

records.className: GE Steam Turbine to Alstom Steam Turbine (ST mechanical x-over) 26-2
records.courseName: I-XSTM30402 GE Steam Turbine to Alstom Steam Turbine (ST mechanical x-over)
records.comment: A respectful and peaceful class environment must be maintained and kept at all times as per GE code of conduct. Students without commitment and respect to instructor caused multiple problems in the class  many times. Those situations happened from the beginning of the training with one student abandoning it. Students not removed from class affected overall training progress  without commitment to hands on activities and being unrespectful to our instructor.    If the business needs to accommodate different positions for training a different course should become available to fulfill all expectations. Allowing enough time for a theoretical class and then the practical  would allow students learn GE x Alstom differences and practice with hands on. Due to limited time (and a few students lack of commitment)  many classes materials had to be quickly viewed.  As a Steam Power employee  training does not deeply show the units we see in the field  being necessary to perform additional trainings if a fleet understanding is needed.

records.comment: HA training was well organized  and successfully provided a solid foundation of HA. Instructors were knowledgeable  and training objectives were generally achieved.  Suggestions for improvement: 1. Intended target audience should clearly defined (experienced/ no HA background)  this will help tailor course content  pace and teaching approach. 2. To include an overview of major HA components  their functions and how differ from conventional GE GT  this help trainees better understand the purpose/ importance of subsequent topics  particularly ITS. 3. Should include more practical FE focused ITS training. Such as purpose of ITS roll-out/ in  ITS clearance taking  pre-roll out inspection and all practical guide based on ITS data sheet GT 9615 and 9610. 4. It is good to have dedicated module covering HA specific special tools. Understanding these tools is essential  as they are one of key diferentiators between HA outagesand conventional GE GT.  5. Final test - 60 questions is appropriate length but the question bank should be reviewed to better reflect practical field scenario and HA knowledge.

records.className: HA FE Tasks & Tools - Combustion Inspection / ITS Rollout & TRACC Scan Alignment 26-4
records.courseName: I-GAS32403 HA FE Tasks & Tools - Combustion Inspection / ITS Rollout & TRACC Scan Alignment
records.comment: 1. Instructors should have more subject matter expertise. Jeff and Tom did well at instructing with the knowledge they had of the tooling however they did not have the subject matter expertise to demonstrate how to properly align the ITS.       2. Get more in depth of the FE roll and responsibilities of removing and aligning the ITS. This class was very much focused on the rolls of the craft and the supervisor. The curriculum overlooked the importance of initial alignment and the use of proper data sheets.   3. Spend time on component identification. There was very little time discussing components during this class. One example of components that should have been mentioned were the seals in ITS and their locations. It was not mentioned in the class of the importance of removing these seals before removing the ITS.   4. Review procedures more in depth and instruct the labs to properly follow the procedure.  This class is 4 weeks long. This time can be better utilized by getting more in depth on an FE level. we could have reviewed procedures better  we could have went over the components more in depth. We did not discuss or review the data sheets for the ITS alignment or where to take the measurements.

records.comment: Air conditioning in the room with the simulators would be good so that we could use them instead of the VR simulators. My credentials to log into the training simulator didn't work for the first 1 1/2 days and then the fix was to use a flash drive from the instructor's login. That only worked for about a day before I started having trouble with the system crashing and having to reboot and constantly buffing. After fighting with those problems I was so far behind the lesson that I ended up just following along with my coworker instead of being able to do the lessons myself. The material that was presented was not what we expecting as far as being advanced troubleshooting. It was basically the same class as what the intermediate class was 9 years ago that we took. For the most part this was a complete waste of our time and our company's money. Cannot believe that a company the size of GE couldn't have enough internet access points that the whole class and others could be on at the same time and not end up buffing about every 10 minutes.

records.className: 26-737 - OEC - Control System - Mark Ve / VIe Troubleshooting (Advanced)
records.courseName: O-CON33401 Control System - Mark Ve / VIe Troubleshooting (Advanced)
records.comment: There are several things I wish this course had. 1: Training on a virtual machine  that doesn't accurately represent what we have in the field isn't helpful. I think I spent more time diagnosing issues with running the simulator and extra steps required to get labs to work than actually learning the material. When the labs aren't working and I'm trying to figure out what I'm doing wrong  and then learn after spending 30 minutes troubleshooting my steps  that the issue is that it's a simulator and that part just doesn't work  it's very frustrating. I have no real confirmation that I completed the lab  because even if it's done right  it just doesn't work. With out class  the virtual machine runs VERY slowly which compounds wasted time and frustration. Throughout the week  the virtual machine was very regularly locking up about every 3 minutes. Basic functionality like clicking buttons on HMI or opening toolbox windows takes far longer in the VM environment than on a real workstation. Poor/inconsistent Wi-Fi seemed to also contribute to disconnect/reconnect issues regularly with the simulator VM and with the screen mirroiring.   2. Course material: About 11 years ago  I took the beginning and intermediate classes and they were great. I was pretty new to the Mark6e controls. The classes got me started and were well structured with defined tabs an the Instruction and lab PAPER BOOKS that I could write notes in  and the course followed the material in the books exactly. The labs built upon each other and the the course material expanded on what was previously learned. In this class  it seemed like there was a lot of overlap  primarily review from the beginning courses. I'd thought that the course would CONTINUE with new material where the intermediate course left off. Instead  it seemed to me like it did a lot of jumping around with material  reviewing basics  and following no structured order.  When doing labs  (on simulators that don't match what the lab states) and doing them in random orders  makes the labs more difficult  because the labs refer to things done in prior labs. If you haven't done the prior labs (because not going in order) and don't have variables created form prior labs in the toolbox software  then you can't actually complete the new labs without modifications. I guess it's good troubleshooting  but difficult for more linear thinkers to jump between labs and complete portions of old labs so you can do the lab assigned.  3. It's hard for me to wrap my head around GE not being able to get an air conditioner put in a building for several months. If you can't provide the class on actual trainers as the class was intended  then cancel the class and give us our money back. Don't stick us in a different room on virtual machines and simulators and pretend like we get the same education.

Appreciated his patience with me on going through associating the whiteboard equations to the actual hands on measurements we got on the machine.

records.className: Laser Alignment Hamar 26-1
records.courseName: I-STM30703 Laser Alignment Hamar
records.comment: I believe the course could be even more effective if it were extended beyond five days. While the current duration provides enough time to become familiar with the tool and understand the theoretical concepts  I think additional hands-on practice would be necessary to build enough confidence and proficiency to use the equipment independently in the field.  One idea would be to provide each student with a complete tool setup and rotate the practical activities among the participants. For example  while part of the group is attending the theoretical sessions  one student could perform the practical exercise and collect their own data. Afterwards  that student could use the data they collected during the theoretical portion of the course  while another student takes their turn completing the practical exercise.  This approach could provide each participant with more individual hands-on experience  reinforce the connection between theory and practice  and help ensure that students feel more confident using the tool when they are required to apply it in the field.
